<style>
/* Layout: a decision strip on top, a stage answer below it, then topic sections, then the evidence library everything links back into. */

*{box-sizing:border-box}
body{background:var(--bg); color:var(--ink); font-family:var(--sans); font-size:15px; line-height:1.55;

h1,h2,h3,h4{font-family:var(--serif); text-wrap:balance; margin:0}

a{color:var(--teal)}

/* header */
header.top{position:sticky; top:env(safe-area-inset-top,0px); z-index:40; background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 92%, transparent);

/* legend */
.legend{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(250px,1fr)); gap:14px; margin-top:22px}
.lg{background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:10px; padding:14px 15px; box-shadow:var(--shadow); min-width:0}
.lg h4{font-size:13px; letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; font-family:var(--sans); color:var(--muted); margin-bottom:9px}

/* label + grade pills */
.pill{display:inline-block; font-size:11px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:.04em; text-transform:uppercase;
  padding:2px 7px; border-radius:5px; border:1px solid; white-space:nowrap}
.p-std{color:var(--navy); border-color:var(--navy); background:var(--navy-soft)}

.grade{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-width:19px; width:auto; padding:0 5px; white-space:nowrap; height:19px; border-radius:4px;
  font-size:11.5px; font-weight:700; border:1px solid var(--line); background:var(--surface2); color:var(--ink); flex:none}
.grade.A{background:var(--navy); color:var(--surface); border-color:var(--navy)}
.grade.B{background:var(--teal); color:var(--surface); border-color:var(--teal)}
.grade.C{background:var(--amber-soft); color:var(--amber); border-color:var(--amber)}
.grade.D{background:transparent; color:var(--muted)}
.flag{font-size:10.5px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:.05em; color:var(--muted); border:1px dashed var(--line);
  border-radius:4px; padding:1px 5px; white-space:nowrap}

/* tree */
.tree{margin-top:14px}
.entry{background:var(--ink); color:var(--bg); border-radius:10px; padding:12px 16px; font-size:13.6px; line-height:1.45}

.qrow{display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:stretch; margin-top:16px}
.q{flex:1 1 0; min-width:0; position:relative; display:flex}
.qbox{flex:1; background:var(--surface); border:2px solid var(--ink); border-radius:10px; padding:12px 13px; display:flex;
  flex-direction:column; gap:7px; min-width:0}
.qhead{font-weight:600; font-size:14.4px; line-height:1.3}
.qans{display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:flex-start; gap:5px; font-size:12.4px; color:var(--muted); margin-top:auto}
.goto{appearance:none; font:inherit; font-size:12.4px; cursor:pointer; background:var(--surface2); color:var(--ink);
  border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:7px; padding:3px 9px; text-align:left; max-width:100%}
.goto:hover{border-color:var(--ink)}
.goto b{font-weight:700}
.qnext{font-size:12.4px; color:var(--muted)}
.arrowR{position:absolute; right:-9px; top:50%; transform:translateY(-50%); color:var(--muted); font-size:15px; line-height:1}
@media (max-width:640px){ .arrowR{display:none} }

/* reference strip: closed items stay inline, the open one takes its own row */
.refstrip{display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:8px; align-items:center; margin-top:12px}
.refstrip > .reflab{font-size:10.5px; letter-spacing:.08em; text-transform:uppercase; font-weight:700; color:var(--muted)}
.refstrip > details{margin-top:0; flex:0 0 auto; min-width:0}
.refstrip > details > summary{font-size:13.5px; padding:7px 14px; gap:8px; border-color:var(--line);
  background:var(--surface); box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
.refstrip > details > summary:hover{background:var(--surface2)}
.refstrip > details[open] > summary{border-color:var(--ink)}
.ricon{width:19px; height:19px; flex:none; order:-1; color:var(--teal)}
.refstrip > details[open] > summary .ricon{color:var(--ink)}
.refstrip > details[open]{flex:1 1 100%}
.refstrip > details[open] > .moreinner{background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:11px;
  padding:14px 16px; margin-top:9px; box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
.cp{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(168px,1fr)); gap:10px; margin-top:10px}
.cp label{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:3px; font-size:12px; font-weight:600; color:var(--muted); min-width:0}
.cp select{font:inherit; font-size:13px; padding:5px 7px; border-radius:7px; border:1px solid var(--line);
  background:var(--surface); color:var(--ink); max-width:100%}
.cpout{margin-top:12px; display:flex; gap:9px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap; font-size:13.5px}
.cpclass{font-family:var(--serif); font-size:19px; font-weight:700}
.minitab{width:100%; min-width:0; border-collapse:collapse; font-size:12.6px; margin-top:10px}
.minitab th,.minitab td{text-align:left; padding:6px 9px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line2); vertical-align:top}
.minitab th{font-size:10.5px; letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); background:var(--surface2)}
.minitab tr:last-child td{border-bottom:0}
.minitab td:first-child{font-weight:600}
.minitab.keys td:first-child{white-space:nowrap; width:1%}
.minitabwrap{overflow-x:auto; margin-top:10px}
.minitabwrap .minitab{min-width:440px; margin-top:0}
.lrgrid{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(260px,1fr)); gap:14px; margin-top:12px}

/* stages */
.stages{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(5,1fr); gap:10px; margin-top:16px}
.st{appearance:none; text-align:left; font:inherit; color:inherit; cursor:pointer; background:var(--surface);
  border:1px solid var(--line); border-left:4px solid var(--line); border-radius:10px; padding:12px 13px; min-width:0;
  display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:5px; box-shadow:var(--shadow); transition:border-color .12s, transform .12s}
.st:hover{transform:translateY(-1px)}
.st .sname{font-family:var(--serif); font-size:17px; font-weight:700; line-height:1.15}
.st .sreq{font-size:10.4px; letter-spacing:.07em; text-transform:uppercase; font-weight:700; color:var(--muted)}
/* ALL vs ANY is the thing a reader must not misread: give the quantifier its
   own colour and keep it uppercase even outside the small-caps label */
.qw{font-weight:800; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.06em; padding:0 4px; border-radius:4px}
.qw.all{color:var(--navy); background:var(--navy-soft)}
.qw.any{color:var(--amber); background:var(--amber-soft)}
.st .scrit{list-style:none; margin:0; padding:0; font-size:12.3px; line-height:1.3; color:var(--muted)}
.st .scrit li{position:relative; padding-left:11px; margin-top:4px}
.st .scrit li:first-child{margin-top:0}
.st .scrit li::before{content:""; position:absolute; left:2px; top:.52em; width:4px; height:1px; background:currentColor; opacity:.65}
.st[data-tone="cure"]{border-left-color:var(--navy)}
.st[data-tone="loco"]{border-left-color:var(--amber)}
.st[data-tone="sys"]{border-left-color:var(--clay)}
.st[data-tone="pall"]{border-left-color:var(--muted)}
.st[aria-pressed="true"]{border-color:var(--ink); box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--ink) inset, var(--shadow)}
.st:focus-visible, .tab:focus-visible, .refchip:focus-visible, button:focus-visible, input:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--teal); outline-offset:2px}

/* answer panel */
.answer{margin-top:16px; background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:12px; box-shadow:var(--shadow);

.ahead{padding:15px 18px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line2); display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:flex-start; flex-wrap:wrap}
.ahead h3{font-size:22px}
.abody{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr); gap:0}
.acol{padding:15px 18px; border-right:1px solid var(--line2); min-width:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:11px}
.acol:last-child{border-right:0}
.acol > .eyebrow{margin-bottom:-3px}
.rec{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:7px; font-size:13.8px; line-height:1.5}
.recmeta{display:flex; gap:6px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap}
.recnote{font-size:12.6px; color:var(--muted); border-left:2px solid var(--line); padding-left:9px}
.opts{display:flex; flex-direction:column}
.opt{display:grid; grid-template-columns:23px 1fr; gap:11px; padding:11px 0; border-top:1px solid var(--line2); min-width:0}
.opt:first-child{border-top:0; padding-top:4px}
.optn{width:23px; height:23px; border-radius:50%; background:var(--surface2); color:var(--muted); font-size:11.5px;
  font-weight:700; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; flex:none}
.optname{font-family:var(--serif); font-size:15.5px; font-weight:700; display:flex; gap:7px; align-items:center;
  flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:4px; line-height:1.2}
.optwhen{font-size:13.5px; line-height:1.45}
details.more{margin-top:8px}
details.more > summary{cursor:pointer; list-style:none; font-size:12px; font-weight:600; color:var(--teal);
  display:inline-flex; gap:6px; align-items:center; padding:4px 11px; border-radius:999px;
  border:1px solid var(--line); background:var(--surface2)}
details.more > summary::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}
details.more > summary::before{content:"Show"; font-weight:700; color:var(--ink)}
details.more[open] > summary::before{content:"Hide"}
details.more > summary:hover{color:var(--ink); border-color:var(--ink)}
details.more > summary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--teal); outline-offset:3px}
.moreinner{padding:2px 0 4px}
.xpand{appearance:none; cursor:pointer; font:inherit; font-size:11.5px; font-weight:600; color:var(--muted);

.xpand:hover{color:var(--ink); border-color:var(--ink)}

.optline.bad .optlab{color:var(--clay)}

.optwhen + .refs{margin-top:6px}
.orderrule{margin-top:11px; font-size:12.8px; color:var(--muted); border-top:1px dashed var(--line); padding-top:10px; line-height:1.5}
.orderrule b{color:var(--ink)}

/* ref chips */
.refs{display:flex; gap:5px; flex-wrap:wrap}
.refchip{appearance:none; cursor:pointer; font:inherit; font-size:11.5px; font-weight:600; padding:1px 7px; border-radius:999px;
  border:1px solid var(--line); background:var(--surface2); color:var(--teal); white-space:nowrap}
.refchip:hover{border-color:var(--teal)}

/* sections */
section{scroll-margin-top:80px}
.sechead{margin-top:46px; display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:baseline; flex-wrap:wrap; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); padding-bottom:9px}
.sechead p{font-size:13.5px; color:var(--muted); max-width:62ch}
.tabs{display:flex; gap:6px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-top:16px}
.tab{appearance:none; cursor:pointer; font:inherit; font-size:13px; font-weight:600; padding:6px 12px; border-radius:999px;
  border:1px solid var(--line); background:var(--surface); color:var(--muted)}
.tab[aria-selected="true"]{background:var(--ink); color:var(--bg); border-color:var(--ink)}
.panel{margin-top:16px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:14px}

.card{background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:11px; padding:16px 18px; box-shadow:var(--shadow); min-width:0}
.card h3{margin-bottom:4px}
.card .kicker{font-size:12.5px; color:var(--muted); margin-bottom:11px}
.card p + p{margin-top:9px}
.stack{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px}
.kv{display:grid; grid-template-columns:auto 1fr; gap:6px 14px; font-size:13.6px; align-items:baseline}
.kv dt{font-weight:600; color:var(--teal); white-space:nowrap}
.kv dd{margin:0; min-width:0}

.tablewrap{overflow-x:auto; border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:11px; background:var(--surface); box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
table{border-collapse:collapse; width:100%; min-width:720px; font-size:13.3px}
th,td{text-align:left; padding:11px 13px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line2); vertical-align:top}
th{font-size:11.5px; letter-spacing:.07em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); font-weight:700; background:var(--surface2); position:sticky; top:0}
tbody tr:last-child td{border-bottom:0}
td b{font-weight:600}

.callout{border-left:3px solid var(--clay); background:var(--clay-soft); border-radius:0 9px 9px 0; padding:13px 16px; font-size:13.6px}
.callout.amber{border-left-color:var(--amber); background:var(--amber-soft)}
.callout.teal{border-left-color:var(--teal); background:var(--teal-soft)}
.callout b{font-weight:700}

/* liver-directed matrix */
:root{ --t1f:#0f5c38; --t1b:#c8e6d3; --t2f:#4b7f1c; --t2b:#eff6df; --t3f:#24609e; --t3b:#dde9f6;
       --t4f:#a15c00; --t4b:#fbe8c9; --t5f:#5b616a; --t5b:#eceef1 }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){ :root:not([data-theme="light"]){
  --t1f:#7fd6a6; --t1b:#16382a; --t2f:#b5dc84; --t2b:#2b3a1a; --t3f:#8dbcf0; --t3b:#1a2c42;
  --t4f:#f2bb6b; --t4b:#3f2e14; --t5f:#b4bac3; --t5b:#2c3036 }}
:root[data-theme="dark"]{
  --t1f:#7fd6a6; --t1b:#16382a; --t2f:#b5dc84; --t2b:#2b3a1a; --t3f:#8dbcf0; --t3b:#1a2c42;
  --t4f:#f2bb6b; --t4b:#3f2e14; --t5f:#b4bac3; --t5b:#2c3036 }
/* the five tiers read left to right as a scale */
.tierlegend{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(5,1fr); gap:8px; margin-top:16px}
.tl{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:7px; font-size:12.2px; line-height:1.4; min-width:0;
  background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:10px; padding:11px 12px 12px;
  box-shadow:var(--shadow); position:relative; overflow:hidden}
.tl::before{content:""; position:absolute; inset:0 0 auto 0; height:4px}
.tl[data-tier="1"]::before{background:var(--t1f)} .tl[data-tier="2"]::before{background:var(--t2f)}
.tl[data-tier="3"]::before{background:var(--t3f)} .tl[data-tier="4"]::before{background:var(--t4f)}
.tl[data-tier="5"]::before{background:var(--t5f)}
.tl > span:last-child{min-width:0; color:var(--muted)}
.tl .tchip{align-self:flex-start; margin-top:3px}
@media (max-width:980px){ .tierlegend{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)} }
@media (max-width:620px){ .tierlegend{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)} }
@media (max-width:420px){ .tierlegend{grid-template-columns:1fr} }
.tchip{font-size:10.5px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:.03em; padding:2px 7px; border-radius:5px; flex:none; max-width:100%}
.mcell .tchip, .rolewhen .tchip{white-space:nowrap}
.t1{color:var(--t1f); background:var(--t1b)} .t2{color:var(--t2f); background:var(--t2b)}
.t3{color:var(--t3f); background:var(--t3b)} .t4{color:var(--t4f); background:var(--t4b)}
.t5{color:var(--t5f); background:var(--t5b)}
/* six modalities side by side */
.mcards{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(6,1fr); gap:8px; margin-top:18px}
.mcell{appearance:none; text-align:left; font:inherit; color:inherit; cursor:pointer; background:var(--surface);

<section id="tree">
  <div class="sechead">
    <h2>The decision tree</h2>
    <p>Three questions in order. Every <b>yes</b> settles the stage; every <b>no</b> moves to the next question. Performance status and spread are therefore decided before tumour burden is ever asked. Choose any answer or any stage to see the full recommendation.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="tree">
    <div class="entry"><b>HCC confirmed</b> — LR-5 on multiphase CT or MRI in an at-risk liver; biopsy when imaging is indeterminate, decided at MDT. <b>Stage with</b> liver imaging and chest CT · ECOG · Child-Pugh and bilirubin · portal hypertension assessment · AFP. Nonresectability and transplant candidacy are assessed in parallel with the rest of staging, not after it.</div>

    <div class="refstrip">
      <span class="reflab">Reference</span>

      <details class="more"><summary><svg class="ricon" viewbox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="4" y="2.5" width="16" height="19" rx="2.5"></rect><rect x="7.5" y="6" width="9" height="3.5" rx="1"></rect><circle cx="8.5" cy="13.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="13.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="15.5" cy="13.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="8.5" cy="17.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="17.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="15.5" cy="17.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle></svg>Child-Pugh</summary><div class="moreinner">
        <p class="small muted">Five parameters, 1–3 points each. <b>Class A 5–6 · Class B 7–9 · Class C 10–15.</b></p>
        <div class="cp">
          <label>Bilirubin (mg/dL)
            <select id="cpBili"><option value="1"><2</option><option value="2">2–3</option><option value="3">>3</option></select></label>
          <label>Albumin (g/dL)
            <select id="cpAlb"><option value="1">>3.5</option><option value="2">2.8–3.5</option><option value="3"><2.8</option></select></label>
          <label>INR
            <select id="cpInr"><option value="1"><1.7</option><option value="2">1.7–2.3</option><option value="3">>2.3</option></select></label>
          <label>Ascites
            <select id="cpAsc"><option value="1">None</option><option value="2">Mild, diuretic-responsive</option><option value="3">Moderate–severe or refractory</option></select></label>
          <label>Encephalopathy
            <select id="cpEnc"><option value="1">None</option><option value="2">Grade I–II</option><option value="3">Grade III–IV</option></select></label>
        </div>
        <div class="cpout"><span class="cpclass" id="cpClass">Class A</span><span class="chip" id="cpPts">5 points</span>
          <span class="small muted" id="cpNote">Preserved function. This does not establish portal pressure — see the portal hypertension assessment.</span></div>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:10px">In primary biliary cholangitis and primary sclerosing cholangitis the bilirubin bands are <4, 4–10 and >10 mg/dL. The roadmap also records ALBI and MELD 3.0; Child-Pugh alone does not drive allocation.</p>
      </div></details>

      <details class="more"><summary><svg class="ricon" viewbox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="5" r="2.6"></circle><path d="M12 7.8v7"></path><path d="M6.5 10.2h11"></path><path d="M12 14.8 8.5 21"></path><path d="m12 14.8 3.5 6.2"></path></svg>ECOG performance status</summary><div class="moreinner">
        <table class="minitab"><thead><tr><th style="width:52px">Grade</th><th>Definition</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>0</td><td>Fully active, able to carry on all pre-disease performance without restriction.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>1</td><td>Restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out work of a light or sedentary nature — light house work, office work.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>2</td><td>Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to carry out any work activities; up and about more than 50% of waking hours.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3</td><td>Capable of only limited self-care; confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>4</td><td>Completely disabled; cannot carry on any self-care; totally confined to bed or chair.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>5</td><td>Dead.</td></tr>
        </tbody></table>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:10px">Oken et al., Am J Clin Oncol 1982. <b>In this pathway ECOG 3–4 settles stage D, and cancer-related ECOG 1–2 is part of stage C</b> — record whether the limitation is from the tumour or the liver, because that distinction decides whether transplantation remains an option.</p>
      </div></details>

      <details class="more"><summary><svg class="ricon" viewbox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3.4"></circle><path d="M12 1.8v3.4M12 18.8v3.4M1.8 12h3.4M18.8 12h3.4"></path></svg>LI-RADS, in full</summary><div class="moreinner">
        <p class="small muted">CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 diagnostic algorithm and the v2024 treatment-response algorithms. <b>Applies only in the at-risk population</b> — cirrhosis of any cause, chronic hepatitis B, or current or prior HCC. OPTN class 5 criteria for listing are a separate system.</p>

        <div class="lrgrid">
          <div>
            <h4 class="eyebrow">The four major features</h4>
            <table class="minitab keys"><tbody>
              <tr><td>Nonrim APHE</td><td>Unequivocal enhancement in the arterial phase, in whole or in part, that is <b>not</b> rim-shaped.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>Nonperipheral washout</td><td>Visually assessed reduction in enhancement relative to liver, in whole or in part, from an earlier to a later phase — not peripheral.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>Enhancing capsule</td><td>Smooth, uniform, sharp border around most or all of the observation, unequivocally thicker or more conspicuous than around background nodules.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>Threshold growth</td><td>≥50% increase in size in ≤6 months.</td></tr>
            </tbody></table>
            <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:8px">Size is the fifth criterion and sets the row of the table; the three features other than APHE are what “additional major features” counts.</p>
          </div>
          <div>
            <h4 class="eyebrow">Other categories</h4>
            <table class="minitab keys"><tbody>
              <tr><td>LR-1</td><td>Definitely benign.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-2</td><td>Probably benign.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-3</td><td>Intermediate probability of malignancy.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-4</td><td>Probably HCC.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-5</td><td>Definitely HCC.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-M</td><td>Probably or definitely malignant, not HCC specific — targetoid appearance or other features favouring cholangiocarcinoma or a combined tumour.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-TIV</td><td>Tumour in vein: enhancing soft tissue within a vessel, whatever the parenchymal observation.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-NC</td><td>Not categorisable because of image degradation or omission.</td></tr>
            </tbody></table>
          </div>
        </div>

        <h4 class="eyebrow" style="margin-top:16px">Diagnostic table — no nonrim APHE (absent, or rim / peripheral discontinuous)</h4>
        <table class="minitab"><thead><tr><th style="width:38%">Additional major features</th><th><20 mm</th><th>≥20 mm</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>0</td><td>LR-3</td><td>LR-3</td></tr>
          <tr><td>1</td><td>LR-3</td><td>LR-4</td></tr>
          <tr><td>≥2</td><td>LR-4</td><td>LR-4</td></tr>
        </tbody></table>

        <h4 class="eyebrow" style="margin-top:14px">Diagnostic table — nonrim APHE present</h4>
        <div class="minitabwrap"><table class="minitab"><thead><tr><th style="width:34%">Additional major features</th><th><10 mm</th><th>10–19 mm</th><th>≥20 mm</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>0</td><td>LR-3</td><td>LR-3</td><td>LR-4</td></tr>
          <tr><td>1</td><td>LR-4</td><td>LR-4 if capsule alone<br>LR-5 if washout or threshold growth</td><td>LR-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td>≥2</td><td>LR-4</td><td>LR-5</td><td>LR-5</td></tr>
        </tbody></table></div>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:8px"><b>An observation under 10 mm cannot be LR-5.</b> LR-5 requires ≥10 mm with nonrim APHE plus nonperipheral washout or threshold growth, or ≥20 mm with nonrim APHE plus any one additional feature.</p>

        <h4 class="eyebrow" style="margin-top:16px">Treatment response v2024 — use the algorithm that matches the treatment</h4>
        <div class="minitabwrap"><table class="minitab"><thead><tr><th style="width:26%">Category</th><th>Nonradiation — ablation, TACE</th><th>Radiation — SBRT, Y-90</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>LR-TR Nonviable</td><td>No lesional enhancement, or treatment-specific expected enhancement.</td><td>No lesional enhancement.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>LR-TR Equivocal</td><td>Enhancement atypical for treatment effect and not meeting viable criteria.</td><td><b>Does not exist</b> in the radiation algorithm.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>LR-TR Nonprogressing</td><td>—</td><td><b>Unique to the radiation algorithm.</b> Persistently enhancing, stable or decreasing — treatment effect rather than residual tumour. Observe with close follow-up; do not retreat on enhancement alone.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>LR-TR Viable</td><td>Nodular, mass-like or thick irregular enhancement in or along the treated lesion.</td><td>New or enlarging mass-like enhancement.</td></tr>
        </tbody></table></div>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:8px">Applying the nonradiation algorithm after radioembolisation or SBRT is a recurring and consequential error in this pathway — it turns expected delayed necrosis into a false call of residual tumour.</p>

        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:12px"><b>Source history.</b> This table is standard reference material, not taken from the roadmap, which cites the ACR documents without reproducing them. Verify against the ACR CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 core and the v2024 treatment-response algorithms before it is used for reporting.</p>
      </div></details>
    </div>

    <div class="qrow" id="qrow">
      <div class="q"><span class="arrowR">→</span><div class="qbox">
        <div class="qhead">ECOG 3–4, or Child-Pugh C and not a transplant candidate?</div>
        <div class="qans">
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="D"><b>Yes →</b> stage D · terminal</button>
          <span class="qnext"><b>No →</b> next question</span>
        </div>
      </div></div>
      <div class="q"><span class="arrowR">→</span><div class="qbox">
        <div class="qhead">Macrovascular invasion, extrahepatic spread, or cancer-related ECOG 1–2?</div>
        <div class="qans">
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="C"><b>Yes →</b> stage C · advanced</button>
          <span class="qnext"><b>No →</b> next question</span>
        </div>
      </div></div>
      <div class="q"><div class="qbox">
        <div class="qhead">With ECOG 0 and preserved liver function, what is the tumour burden?</div>
        <div class="qans">
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="0">Solitary ≤2 cm <b>→</b> stage 0</button>
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="A">Solitary any size, or ≤3 nodules each ≤3 cm <b>→</b> stage A</button>
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="B">Multinodular beyond A <b>→</b> stage B</button>
        </div>
      </div></div>
    </div>

    <p class="small muted">Assess liver function before assigning stages 0–B. Child-Pugh B or decompensation needs individualized hepatology and transplant assessment; tumour burden alone does not establish an early stage or treatment eligibility.</p>
    <div class="stages" id="stageBtns"></div>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="stage">
  <div class="answer" id="answer"></div>
  <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:10px">Stage migration is permitted when anatomy, biology, liver function, transplant strategy, comorbidity, access or patient goals make the stage default unsuitable — the reason must be recorded. It is not a licence to substitute a lower-evidence modality for a proven curative option.</p>
</section>

<section id="lrt">
  <div class="sechead">
    <h2>Liver-directed therapy</h2>
    <p><a href="../lrt/" style="display:inline-block;padding:10px 0;font-weight:700">Open the liver-directed therapy matrix across all five tumor types →</a></p>
    <p>Intent is assigned before a device is chosen. Curative intent means an attempt to eradicate all known cancer; it does not establish a cure rate. Local control, complete radiographic response, complete pathologic necrosis in a treated lesion, and overall survival are four different outcomes.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card" style="margin-top:16px">
    <h3>Choose treatment by its goal and suitability</h3>
    <p>Do not use a universal ablation → SBRT → Y-90 → TACE → HAI → histotripsy sequence. <b>An upfront alternative chosen because of anatomy or organ reserve is not a post-progression second line.</b> Bridge and downstaging preserve a later transplant or resection opportunity; conversion treatment is not itself the curative operation.</p>
    <p>Compare resection, local ablation and transplant where appropriate at multidisciplinary review, and record the intended outcome, why alternatives fit or do not fit, the systemic-treatment plan, the reassessment date and the next action. After progression or toxicity, restage and reconsider complete treatment rather than automatically repeating the same procedure.</p>
    <p class="small muted">The tiers below are a clinical synthesis of treatment intent. They are not the roadmap's A–D evidence grading system, and the two should not be read as equivalent.</p>
  </div>

<section id="ops">
  <div class="sechead">
    <h2>Team responsibilities and quality monitoring</h2>
    <p>Sections 9, 10 and 12 of the roadmap, plus the ratification list. These are stakeholder-derived operating requirements — <b>evidence grade D by construction</b>, local policy choices with no comparative outcome evidence. They are labelled Standard because the programme chose them, not because trials support them, and should be audited for adherence rather than effectiveness until the registry can support an effectiveness question.</p>

  <p><b>Batch 08, 7 October 2026.</b> All 71 papers in the HCC depot were read in full and abstracted, each with the limitations the authors state themselves and an independent critique of what the text supports but the authors do not raise. {id:"cure", name:"Curative", html:`
<div class="card">
  <h3>Resection</h3>
  <p class="kicker"><span class="pill p-std">Standard</span> <span class="grade A">A</span> <span class="flag">EXPERTISE</span>   Localised HCC with technically complete resection, adequate future remnant, preserved function and acceptable portal-hypertension risk.</p>
  <p>In selected multifocal or larger tumours, resectability is determined by expert hepatobiliary review rather than size alone. After resection, obtain multiphase liver imaging and chest imaging every 3–6 months and continue long-term surveillance, because recurrence risk persists indefinitely.</p>
  <div class="callout"><b>AASLD advises against routine neoadjuvant or adjuvant systemic therapy for resection or local ablation; use clinical trials.</b> The updated IMbrave050 analysis lost the recurrence-free survival signal seen at the first interim analysis (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.72–1.12), with overall survival immature and numerically unfavourable (HR 1.26). {{37871608|41580093|39992051}}</div>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Establishing clinically significant portal hypertension</h3>
  <p class="kicker">Child-Pugh class, MELD and the absence of decompensation establish preserved hepatic function. They do not establish portal pressure.</p>
  <p>BCLC treats the two as separate axes. A patient can be Child-Pugh A with a normal MELD and still have CSPH — this is the most common way the resection decision is made on incomplete information. CSPH is an HVPG ≥10 mmHg. BCLC accepts surrogate markers, cites Baveno VII for them and keeps HVPG as the gold standard; the table below applies the later Baveno VIII statements. {{41151697|42624290|35120736}}</p>
  <details class="more" open><summary>The Baveno criteria, in full</summary><div class="moreinner">
  <div class="tablewrap"><table><thead><tr><th style="width:18%">Criterion</th><th style="width:38%">Finding</th><th>Interpretation</th></tr></thead><tbody>
   <tr><td><b>Reference standard</b></td><td>HVPG ≥10 mmHg.</td><td>Defines CSPH. BCLC states HVPG remains the gold standard; non-invasive tools may rule it in or out. Measure it when the decision turns on it.</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Specific signs</b></td><td>Oesophageal or gastric varices; spontaneous portosystemic collaterals.</td><td>Baveno VIII identifies varices and portosystemic collaterals as generally indicating CSPH (statement 3.2d), with the exceptions below. The PSVD diagnostic score is a separate assessment; its spleen-stiffness >40 kPa item must not be used to rule in cirrhotic CSPH.</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Non-specific</b></td><td>Platelets <150 × 10⁹/L; splenomegaly.</td><td>Supportive findings do not establish CSPH alone. Ascites requires evaluation for hepatic decompensation and its cause. Absence of these findings does not exclude CSPH.</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Non-invasive rule-in</b></td><td>Liver stiffness ≥25 kPa, except in obese (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) MASLD; spleen stiffness (100 Hz) >55 kPa; ANTICIPATE or ANTICIPATE-NASH ≥75%; NICER ≥75%.</td><td>Baveno VIII statement 1.16 criteria for CSPH in compensated advanced chronic liver disease. In BCLC 0–A HCC without a >5 cm right-lobe nodule, ANTICIPATE or ANTICIPATE-NASH ≥75% is rated only as <b>highly suggestive</b> (statement 1.23, weak recommendation). Useful where HVPG is unavailable or declined — measure HVPG when the resection decision turns on it. <span class="flag">EXPERTISE</span></td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>What to record</b></td><td>The criterion used, its value, and the date.</td><td>“No portal hypertension” without a stated basis is not an acceptable entry when resection is being proposed.</td></tr>
  </tbody></table></div>
  </div></details>
  <details class="more"><summary>Three situations where a portosystemic shunt does not settle the question</summary><div class="moreinner">
  <p style="margin-top:4px"><i>Cured or controlled aetiology</i> — Baveno VIII states varices and collaterals may persist despite resolution of CSPH where the aetiology has been cured or controlled, and after recompensation they are not reliable indicators; in suppressed hepatitis B, cured hepatitis C or sustained alcohol abstinence a shunt alone does not establish current CSPH, so measure. <i>Portosinusoidal vascular disorder</i> — Baveno VII directs that when signs of portal hypertension are present with HVPG <10 mmHg, PSVD must be ruled out; the same imaging finding then carries a different diagnosis and a different operative risk. <i>Steatotic liver disease</i> — BCLC notes HVPG reliability may be suboptimal here, and signs of portal hypertension can occur with HVPG <10 mmHg in a minority of MASH cirrhosis; a sub-threshold measurement should not override a specific sign.</p>
  </div></details>
  <div class="callout amber" style="margin-top:14px"><b>Unresolved locally.</b> Whether a large spontaneous shunt can decompress the portal system enough to lower measured HVPG is a physiological concern raised in practice that this roadmap has not verified against a primary source. Hepatology should rule on it before a sub-10 value is treated as reassuring.</div>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Does CSPH bar resection? The randomised evidence cuts both ways</h3>
  <p>Portal pressure has been prognostic for post-resection decompensation since Bruix 1996. {{8831597}} A meta-analysis of 11 studies quantified it: CSPH assessed by any method raised 3-year post-resection mortality (pooled OR 2.09, 95% CI 1.52–2.88), 5-year mortality (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.51–2.84) and early clinical decompensation (OR 3.04, 95% CI 2.02–4.59). {{25212123}} A hierarchical analysis of decompensation predictors reached the same conclusion. {{27248425}} BCLC's position is that with CSPH resection poses significant risk and transplantation offers better survival.</p>
  <p>The first multicentre randomised test compared partial hepatectomy with ablation, with or without TACE, in HBV-related HCC within Milan criteria and with CSPH (n = 80 per arm). Five-year overall survival was 69.5% with resection versus 64.9% (P = 0.325) and recurrence-free survival 46.2% versus 45.0% (P = 0.783) — no significant difference, in a trial too small to establish equivalence. Total complications were higher after resection (67.5% versus 20%, P < 0.001) but the excess was mainly Clavien-Dindo grade I; grade III–V complications occurred in 8/80 (10%) versus 2/80 (2.5%), with limited power for this comparison. Patients at high risk of postoperative failure were deliberately excluded. These data support selected discussion, not a general claim that resection is safe whenever CSPH is present. {{39322951}}</p>
  <div class="callout teal"><b>The roadmap adopts neither reading by default.</b> CSPH raises operative risk and should trigger transplant assessment in any patient within Milan criteria, but it is not an automatic bar where the remnant is adequate, the resection is minor or laparoscopic, and the hepatologist concurs. <b>Record which reading the board applied.</b> <span class="flag">EXPERTISE</span> <span class="flag">TX-TIMING</span></div>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Thermal ablation</h3>
  <p class="kicker"><span class="pill p-std">Standard</span> <span class="grade A">A</span>   Tumours ≤3 cm, up to three nodules, when a circumferential ablative margin can be achieved safely.</p>
  <p><b>Microwave versus radiofrequency.</b> MWA and RFA are both options. Sugimoto 2025 found lower two-year lesion-level local progression with MWA than single-needle RFA (20/122, 16.4%, versus 38/125, 30.4%; RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.33–0.87; P=.007), without a demonstrated overall-survival advantage. Most lesions were small; this does not establish superiority over every RFA system or a specific 3–4 cm subgroup. The earlier Vietti Violi superiority trial did not show a significant local-progression difference and did not test equivalence. {{29503247|39802807}}</p>
  <p><b>Resection versus ablation for small HCC.</b> The randomised SURF trial (308 registered, 301 analysed — 150 resection, 151 ablation; tumours ≤3 cm, up to three nodules, Child-Pugh ≤7) did not demonstrate superior recurrence-free survival for resection, but non-inferiority was not formally established and the trial was underpowered. The evidence supports the conclusion that for this phenotype the two are reasonable alternatives selected on anatomy, reserve and access — not that they are proven equivalent. {{35949295}}</p>
  <p>Use adjunctive technique or another modality for lesions abutting central bile ducts, bowel, gallbladder, diaphragm, heart or major vessels where a heat sink is expected. For tumours of 3–5 cm, single-probe thermal ablation alone should not be presented as curative-intent therapy.</p>
</div>`},

{id:"tx", name:"Transplant & allocation", html:`
<div class="card">
  <h3>Four kinds of statement, which the roadmap must not blur</h3>
  <dl class="kv">
   <dt>OPTN policy</dt><dd>Binding, and changes without notice to this document. Every numeric criterion must be re-verified against the current Policy 9 text before it is applied to a listing decision. {{OPTN9}}</dd>
   <dt>OPTN guidance</dt><dd>Nonbinding. Informs but does not compel the review board.</dd>
   <dt>Published evidence</dt><dd>MERITS-LT and XXL support downstaging as a strategy, but were generated under earlier allocation rules. {{34331914|32615109}}</dd>
   <dt>Local policy</dt><dd>May be stricter than OPTN policy and is the operative constraint at this centre. Where these conflict, the stricter of OPTN and local policy governs.</dd>
  </dl>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Eligibility pathways</h3>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table><thead><tr><th style="width:20%">Pathway</th><th>Criteria and action</th><th style="width:16%">Source type</th></tr></thead><tbody>
   <tr><td><b>Milan clinical criteria and OPTN T2 exception criteria</b></td><td>One lesion ≥2 cm and ≤5 cm, or 2–3 lesions each ≥1 cm and ≤3 cm; no macrovascular invasion; no extrahepatic spread. <b>The ≥2 cm and ≥1 cm lower limits are OPTN T2 rules</b> — Milan (Mazzaferro 1996) set upper limits only and excluded any vascular or lymph-node invasion. Lesions must meet OPTN class 5 imaging criteria. A solitary lesion <2 cm is T1 and does not attract exception points. Exception points accrue after the required waiting period and are capped relative to the median MELD at transplant in the acquisition circle.</td><td class="small">OPTN policy — verify current text</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Downstaging pool</b><br><span class="small muted">UNOS-DS</span></td><td>One lesion >5 cm and ≤8 cm; or 2–3 lesions each ≤5 cm with at least one lesion >3 cm and total diameter ≤8 cm; or 4–5 lesions each <3 cm with total diameter ≤8 cm. No macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic spread. Viable disease must be downstaged to within Milan and remain there for the required observation period. <b>v0.2 omitted the “at least one lesion >3 cm” qualifier in the 2–3 lesion group, which would have incorrectly routed T2 disease into the downstaging pool.</b></td><td class="small">OPTN policy — verify current text</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>AFP rule</b></td><td>An AFP above 1,000 ng/mL blocks the standard exception until it falls below 500 ng/mL following locoregional therapy. A rise to 500 ng/mL or above at any later point requires review-board referral rather than automatic continuation. Record every AFP value with its date and the intervening treatment.</td><td class="small">OPTN policy — verify current text</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic spread</b></td><td>Excludes the standardized HCC exception. NLRB guidance permits consideration of selected treated primary portal-vein branch invasion or ruptured HCC after at least 12 months of stability; main portal-vein or hepatic-vein invasion remains a contraindication. See the <a href="../transplant/hcc/">transplant assessment pathway</a> for the separate nonstandard review.</td><td class="small">OPTN policy</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Beyond the downstaging pool</b><br><span class="small muted">“all-comers”</span></td><td>Not an automatic exception route and not a recognised standard. Consider only for selected patients through transplant governance and the national liver review board, or within a clinical protocol, using sustained response and tumour biology rather than anatomy alone. Outcomes must be tracked prospectively.</td><td class="small">Local policy + registry</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Checkpoint exposure before transplant</b></td><td>Does not categorically exclude transplant, but the rejection risk and the required washout interval are unresolved; reported allograft rejection after pre-transplant checkpoint exposure is substantial and has been fatal. Require transplant-specific multidisciplinary review and a documented washout and immunosuppression plan agreed <b>before</b> the first dose, not after. Do not use checkpoint inhibitors as a casual bridging strategy. <span class="flag">TX-TIMING</span></td><td class="small">Evidence (low) + local policy</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Post-transplant checkpoint blockade</b></td><td><span class="pill p-avoid">Avoid</span> outside exceptional governance review. Pooled series report graft rejection in a substantial minority with appreciable graft loss and mortality. {{36102312}}</td><td class="small">Evidence (low)</td></tr>
  </tbody></table></div>
  <p style="margin-top:12px"><b>Refer early</b> — when within Milan criteria, when the downstaging pool may apply, or when recurrent HCC combined with the severity of the underlying liver disease makes resection or ablation a poor long-term solution. Repeated locoregional procedures while transplant referral is pending can delay assessment and reduce liver reserve. Refer early.</p>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Listing and allocation — calculated MELD initially, then MMaT-3</h3>
  <p class="kicker">OPTN Policy 9.5.I, full PDF pp. 196–199; guidance pp. 3–4, 7. Policy 9.4.C–E, full PDF pp. 188–189. Official policy checked 1 October 2026.</p>
  <dl class="kv">
   <dt>Authority</dt><dd>Policy 9.5 defines standardized exceptions; the Adult MELD Exceptions for Transplant Oncology document is review-board guidance, not policy and not a clinical standard of care. HCC and perihilar cholangiocarcinoma have standardized routes. Clinical candidacy and local protocol approval remain separate from allocation eligibility.</dd>
   <dt>MMaT</dt><dd>Median MELD at transplant for the donor hospital used in the match run — not one fixed national score. Under Policy 9.4.E an MMaT-relative exception below 15 is assigned 15. Exceptions generally require 90-day extensions (9.4.C).</dd>
   <dt>Route and score</dt><dd>Initial request and first extension receive calculated MELD; any extension after the first receives MMaT-3 (Table 9-10). Because each exception is valid for 90 days (Policy 9.4.A), two consecutive periods at calculated MELD elapse before MMaT-3 applies — approximately six months. <b>Policy states the score table, not a six-month rule.</b> Do not represent successful downstaging or referral as immediate exception points. The scores apply to candidates at least 18 years old at registration; Table 9-10 assigns a different score to a candidate registered between 12 and 18.</dd>
   <dt>Initial eligibility</dt><dd>Before locoregional treatment document lesion number and size on CT or MRI, qualifying Class 5 imaging or biopsy, initial chest CT, absence of extrahepatic spread and macrovascular invasion, nonresectability, AFP, and previous treatment. Standard T2 is one lesion 2–5 cm inclusive, or two to three lesions each 1–3 cm inclusive, with AFP ≤1000 ng/mL. Policy inclusive bounds govern; stricter inequalities in guidance examples do not replace them.</dd>
   <dt>Extensions</dt><dd>Every extension documents CT/MRI stage, treatment if tumour number fell, and AFP. Policy 9.5.I.i item 3 (full PDF p. 196) requires a chest CT only before an <b>initial</b> exception request and states it is not required for extensions; clinically indicated thoracic surveillance is a separate plan.</dd>
   <dt>Beyond-entry</dt><dd>Requires nonstandard review: T2 response, no extrahepatic disease, no macrovascular invasion, no AFP >1000, imaging at least four weeks after the last downstaging treatment, and six months from the first exception request.</dd>
   <dt>After transplant</dt><dd>Submit explant pathology within 60 days as required by Policy 9.5.I. Record graft outcome, recurrence surveillance and the accountable clinical team.</dd>
  </dl>
</div>`},

{id:"loco", name:"Locoregional", html:`
<div class="card">
  <h3>Decision sequence</h3>
  <div class="callout" style="margin-bottom:12px"><b>Do not use a universal ablation → SBRT → Y-90 → TACE → HAI → histotripsy sequence.</b> An upfront alternative chosen because of anatomy or organ reserve is not a post-progression second line.</div>
  <p>Compare resection, local ablation and transplant where appropriate at multidisciplinary review. Record the intended outcome, why alternatives fit or do not fit, the systemic-treatment plan, the reassessment date and the next action. After progression or toxicity, restage and reconsider complete treatment rather than automatically repeating the same procedure. <b>Device availability and specialty preference are not indications.</b></p>
  <p>Evidence differs by indication: radiation segmentectomy and ablative SBRT may be definitive treatments in localized HCC, while broader arterial therapy usually seeks control or conversion. Do not generalize findings from advanced-disease systemic-combination trials to small-tumour definitive therapy.</p>
</div>
<div class="tablewrap">
  <table><thead><tr><th style="width:13%">Modality</th><th style="width:10%">Label</th><th style="width:19%">Preferred phenotype</th><th style="width:19%">Caution or avoid</th><th>Comparative evidence and what governs selection</th></tr></thead><tbody id="locoBody"></tbody></table>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Stop and switch rules</h3>
  <p>After each locoregional treatment, reassess liver function, clinical recovery, AFP trajectory, new disease, and whether a viable target remains — not simply whether another procedure is technically possible.</p>
  <p><b>Switch away</b> from repeated TACE or broad embolisation for new decompensation, worsening ALBI or Child-Pugh, inability to achieve selective access, progression outside the treated territory, new macrovascular or extrahepatic progression, or inadequate response despite technically adequate treatment, assessed after each session. After one or two consecutive treatments without response, consider alternatives in MDT; document any reason to continue a curative or downstaging strategy.</p>
  <p><b>For radiation-based therapy, allow the expected delayed response pattern.</b> Apply the LI-RADS treatment response radiation algorithm and do not declare failure from persistent enhancement alone when the lesion is categorised as nonprogressing. Using the nonradiation algorithm after radioembolisation or SBRT is a recurring and consequential error. {{LIRADS}}</p>
  <p>Every repeat cycle must name, in the note: the viable target, the expected benefit, the liver-function cost, the owner, and the reassessment date.</p>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Portal-vein tumour thrombus</h3>
  <p>Systemic therapy is the default backbone <span class="grade A">A</span>. Adding radioembolisation or external beam radiotherapy is a <span class="pill p-reas">Reasonable</span> consideration <span class="grade B">B</span> when the anatomy is liver-confined, reserve is preserved, dosimetry is feasible, and there is a symptom-control, local-control or protocol-driven goal.</p>
  <p>The supporting randomised data for combined radiotherapy here come from a small single-centre trial against sorafenib, and RTOG 1112 also used a sorafenib comparator; neither has been repeated against a modern immunotherapy backbone. {{29543938|39699905}}</p>
  <div class="callout"><b>Document explicitly why local therapy is being added and when systemic therapy starts or resumes.</b> The most common harm in this group is a delayed systemic start, not the radiation itself.</div>
</div>`},

{id:"resp", name:"Response assessment", html:`
<div class="card">
  <h3>Response assessment</h3>
  <p class="kicker">The response-assessment framework is expert consensus, grade C/D — not randomised evidence. v0.2's figure graded this step A; that is corrected.</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table><thead><tr><th style="width:16%">Treatment</th><th style="width:16%">First assessment</th><th style="width:30%">Framework</th><th>Mandatory return question</th></tr></thead><tbody>
   <tr><td><b>Ablation or TACE</b></td><td>About 4–6 weeks</td><td>LI-RADS treatment response, <b>nonradiation</b> algorithm v2024; AFP and liver function.</td><td>Complete response? Residual viable target? New untreated disease? Is retreatment safe?</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Radioembolisation or SBRT</b></td><td>Usually 8–12 weeks, then serially</td><td>LI-RADS treatment response, <b>radiation</b> algorithm v2024; recognise the nonprogressing category and expect delayed necrosis.</td><td>Is enhancement decreasing or stable, or truly progressing? Is liver function preserved?</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Systemic therapy</b></td><td>Every 6–12 weeks by regimen and tempo</td><td>RECIST 1.1 for trials and extrahepatic disease; mRECIST may supplement assessment of intrahepatic viable tumour but should not drive a switch decision alone.</td><td>Continue, manage toxicity, add local control, switch line, or move to symptom-focused care?</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Transplant waitlist</b></td><td>At least every 3 months</td><td>Viable tumour burden, AFP and its trajectory, vascular and extrahepatic status, exception status.</td><td>Still within criteria? Bridge or downstage needed? Internal hold? Who owns the next step?</td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>After complete response</b></td><td>Every 3–6 months for two years, then every six months, at least five years</td><td>Multiphase liver CT or MRI, chest imaging as appropriate, AFP with its trend. Care for the underlying liver disease continues alongside.</td><td>New lesion, rising AFP, or change in liver function — back to MDT? Which option now applies?</td></tr>
  </tbody></table></div>
  <p style="margin-top:12px">Every reassessment returns to the MDT when there is viable tumour, discordant interpretation, a new lesion, stage migration, treatment toxicity, a change in transplant eligibility, or uncertainty about the next modality.</p>
</div>`}
];

  "One randomised trial supports it.
