Crude HCC incidence was 37% higher in the screened arm (rate ratio 1.37, 95% CI 0.99 to 1.89), which the authors read as over-diagnosis. The population was HBsAg carriers aged 35 to 59 in Shanghai, mostly without documented cirrhosis. All evidence in cirrhosis is observational.",
  "Whether any HCC treatment, including transplant, would be offered at all; competing mortality from the liver disease; the patient's own view of a 0.5-year lead time and of over-diagnosis.",
  "Proportion of surveillance orders left open in patients for whom no treatment would be offered; visualisation score recorded separately from the ultrasound category."],
 ["LI-RADS gives a diagnosis of HCC without tissue.",
  "LR-5 as a non-invasive diagnostic standard rests on guideline consensus, not on a randomised or prospectively validated comparison against pathology in this population. The LI-RADS treatment-response algorithms, including the separate radiation algorithm this roadmap insists on, have no outcome validation at all; the page already grades the response framework C to D. AASLD calls its own document a guidance, with no mandatory systematic review, no GRADE and several Strong Recommendations resting on Level 5 expert opinion.",
  "Whether a wrong call would change the plan now: transplant listing, an imminent resection, or a suspicion of non-HCC malignancy.",
  "Cases where the nonradiation algorithm was applied after radioembolisation or SBRT; LR-4 and LR-M cases whose tissue was obtained before transplant discussion."],
 ["Clinically significant portal hypertension predicts decompensation after resection, so resection should be reconsidered when it is present.",
  "The index study is 29 patients with 11 events and 44 candidate variables screened: HVPG odds ratio 1.90 per mmHg (95% CI 1.12 to 3.22), with unresolved decompensation in 11 of 15 patients at an HVPG of 10 mmHg or more and 0 of 14 below it, a separation too clean to reproduce. The meta-analysis that quantified it pooled crude, unadjusted estimates from 11 mostly retrospective single-centre studies: 3-year mortality odds ratio 2.09 (95% CI 1.52 to 2.88), 5-year 2.07 (1.51 to 2.84), early decompensation 3.04 (2.02 to 4.59). The effect size depends on how CSPH was measured, from 8.00 (2.59 to 24.69) in HVPG-based studies to 1.76 (1.38 to 2.25) with surrogate markers, and the HVPG decompensation subgroup is three small studies with a confidence interval of 2.81 to 80.06.",
  "Extent of hepatectomy, future liver remnant, MELD, and whether the patient is within Milan and could be transplanted instead.",
  "Every resection proposal records which criterion established or excluded CSPH, its value and its date; decompensation at 90 days by remnant and by extent of resection."],
 ["The only randomised test shows resection is safe in clinically significant portal hypertension.",
  "Yuan 2024 randomised 160 HBV-related patients within Milan, 80 per arm, and found 5-year overall survival of 69.5% after hepatectomy versus 64.9% after ablation with or without TACE (HR 1.29, 95% CI 0.78 to 2.12, P = 0.325) and recurrence-free survival of 46.2% versus 45.0% (P = 0.783). A confidence interval from 0.78 to 2.12 cannot exclude a two-fold difference either way, and the trial was powered for a superiority it did not find. CSPH was diagnosed by platelet count, splenomegaly, vessel calibre and varices; no HVPG was measured anywhere in the trial, so it is not anchored to the 10 mmHg threshold the BCLC rule rests on. Of 2,077 patients screened, 160 were randomised, 98.7% and 96.2% were Child-Pugh A and the mean tumour was 2.6 cm.",
  "Which reading of CSPH the board has adopted; whether the planned resection is minor or laparoscopic; aetiology, since this trial is entirely hepatitis B.",
  "Decompensation and Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher complications in resected patients with a recorded CSPH criterion."],
 ["Non-invasive testing can rule clinically significant portal hypertension in or out in a surgical candidate with HCC.",
  "Baveno VIII's three HCC-specific statements are all new, graded level of evidence 3 with weak strength, at 94% faculty agreement; they are expert consensus, not prospectively validated practice. The rule-out combination of liver stiffness 15 kPa or less with platelets of 150 x 10 to the 9th per litre or more carries a negative predictive value above 90% in compensated advanced chronic liver disease, but the thresholds are device- and technique-specific, are not validated in obese MASLD, and the faculty's own research agenda still lists the prognostic role of HVPG before surgery as unresolved. In macrovascular invasion the faculty state non-invasive tests may not be applicable at all.",
  "Whether the resection decision actually turns on portal pressure, in which case measure HVPG; aetiology and BMI; whether a shunt reflects current or historical physiology.",
  "Proportion of resection decisions made on a non-invasive criterion where HVPG was available and not measured."],
 ["Resection and thermal ablation are equivalent for small HCC.",
  "No trial has shown equivalence. SURF-RCT closed at 302 of a planned 600 patients, leaving 67.2% power, and reported 5-year overall survival of 74.6% versus 70.4% (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.43) and recurrence-free survival of 42.9% versus 42.7% (HR 0.90, 0.67 to 1.22). Local control was not equal: recurrence at the treated site was 12 of 150 (8.0%) after resection versus 24 of 152 (15.8%) after ablation (P = 0.03), and 19 of 382 (5.0%) versus 49 of 371 (13.2%) in the parallel cohort. The population was far narrower than the entry criteria: 90% solitary, about 65% no larger than 2.0 cm, median 1.8 cm, with tumours near vessels, bile ducts or adjacent organs excluded as unfeasible for ablation. Chen 2006 is quoted for the same claim but 19 of its 90 ablation patients (21%) withdrew and had resection instead, and a single RFA session achieved complete necrosis in only 62.0%.",
  "Tumour size and location, achievable circumferential margin, hepatic reserve and portal pressure, and whether salvage of a local recurrence will actually be available.",
  "Local recurrence at the treated site by modality and by size band; proportion of 3 to 5 cm tumours treated with single-probe ablation and called curative-intent."],
 ["Microwave ablation is preferred over radiofrequency ablation.",
  "The earlier Vietti Violi comparison was a superiority trial that did not show superiority and did not test non-inferiority: 2-year local tumour progression in 6 of 98 lesions (6%) after microwave versus 12 of 104 (12%) after radiofrequency, risk ratio 1.62 (95% CI 0.66 to 3.94), P = 0.27, with 2-year overall survival of 86% versus 84%. Mean lesion size was 18 mm and only 11 lesions measured 3 to 4 cm, which is the size range where microwave is argued to help. The analysis was per protocol, one device was used throughout, and the manufacturer funded the trial. The later Sugimoto trial supports a device-specific local-control advantage for MWA, without a demonstrated survival advantage (PMID 39802807).",
  "Tumour size, proximity to large vessels, expected procedure time, operator familiarity.",
  "Local tumour progression at 12 and 24 months by device."],
 ["Thermal ablation achieves near-complete local control in very early HCC.",
  "The 97.2% sustained complete response (212 of 218) comes from a retrospective multicentre cohort with no control group, and it sits alongside 5-year disease-free survival of 20% (95% CI 7 to 36) and 80% recurrence at 5 years. Operability was assigned retrospectively from age and laboratory criteria rather than by surgical assessment, and the 5-year survival of 68% quoted against surgery is from the selected 100 of 218 patients called operable. Fourteen of 232 otherwise eligible patients (6.0%) could not be treated because the tumour sat in a high-risk area or was poorly visible on ultrasound, which are the tumours hardest to ablate.",
  "Background liver disease rather than the index lesion, since it governs the recurrence that follows; whether transplant is the better long-term answer.",
  "Local control and overall recurrence reported separately; proportion of cases abandoned for poor visibility or unsafe route."],
 ["Milan criteria identify the patients who do well after transplant.",
  "The criteria were derived and validated in the same 48-patient cohort with only 4 recurrences, and the authors state the analyses of T stage, nodule number and AFP had very low power. Four-year overall survival was 75% and recurrence-free survival 83% overall, but the 85% versus 50% separation that defines the criteria was obtained by applying them to explant pathology, not to preoperative imaging: 13 of 48 patients (27%) were understaged before surgery despite angiography and CT arterial portography. Median follow-up was 26 months with only 5 patients still at risk at 48 months. There is no external validation, and the era had no MELD allocation, no AFP selection and a 143-day median wait. The lower bounds on the page, a lesion of 2 cm or more and lesions of 1 cm or more, are OPTN T2 allocation rules; Milan set upper limits only.",
  "Explant risk the imaging cannot see, AFP and its trajectory, the severity of the underlying liver disease, and current waiting-list behaviour at this centre.",
  "Explant stage against last pre-transplant imaging stage, reported as an understaging rate; recurrence by whether explant was within or beyond Milan."],
 ["Downstaging into Milan criteria selects favourable biology.",
  "It selects imaging response, which is not the same thing. In MERITS-LT, 174 of 209 patients (83.3%) were downstaged to within Milan, but cumulative dropout was 22.5% at 1 year and 37.3% at 2 years, and on explant 42.8% were beyond Milan and 17.5% had microvascular invasion, twice the rate of earlier reports. Only 63 patients (30.1%) were transplanted, with post-transplant follow-up of a median 1.7 years and recurrence in 5 of 63 (7.9%); intention-to-treat survival was 92.5% at 1 year and 73.0% at 3 years. The authors conclude Milan criteria should be a minimum requirement, not a sufficient one. The cohort also predates the current median-MELD-minus-3 rule, so its dropout and transplant probabilities do not describe present waiting-list behaviour.",
  "Total tumour burden and its trend, AFP and AFP-L3, time held within criteria, and the competing claim of non-cancer candidates on the same graft.",
  "Dropout and understaging rates in our own downstaged patients; number of locoregional procedures per patient before listing."],
 ["The XXL trial shows transplant beats continued locoregional therapy after downstaging.",
  "XXL closed at 45 of a planned 260 patients after Italian allocation policy changed, so the 5-year survival of 77.5% versus 31.2% (published HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.92) rests on 21 deaths against a prespecified 87, with a conditional power calculation substituted for the missing events. The control arm was unstandardised best available therapy chosen per centre between 2011 and 2015, when sorafenib was the only systemic option, so a 31.2% comparator may understate what current systemic therapy achieves. Downstaging itself was centre-specific, TACE alone in 49%, so the 73% success rate is not a reproducible protocol, and tumour burden had rebounded from a median of 0 at randomisation to 4.8 on explant.",
  "What the realistic alternative to transplant is for this patient today, not in 2015; graft availability; the response achieved and how long it has held.",
  "Outcomes of patients downstaged and listed versus downstaged and not listed, tracked prospectively."],
 ["The AFP rule is a single clear threshold.",
  "Two guidelines give different rules and neither threshold was derived from a trial. EASL 2025 makes an AFP above 1,000 ng/mL an absolute contraindication whatever the tumour burden and requires AFP below 1,000 for at least 3 months after downstaging; OPTN policy uses AFP above 1,000 followed by reduction below 500 ng/mL after treatment; AASLD’s guidance uses 1,000 or more. The current OPTN policy governs standardized exception scoring, which is distinct from listing. In the Milan cohort an AFP above or below 300 ng/mL was not significantly related to survival or recurrence, on 4 recurrences. In MERITS-LT the only independent predictor of dropout was a pre-treatment AFP-L3 of 10% or more, sub-hazard ratio 3.7 (95% CI 1.27 to 10.79), and it was measured in only 83 of 209 patients. BCLC 2026 still names no AFP decline that qualifies a downstaged patient.",
  "Which policy actually binds this listing, the trajectory rather than a single value, and what treatment lay between the values.",
  "Every AFP recorded with its date and the intervening treatment; review-board referrals triggered by a rise to 500 ng/mL or above."],
 ["Exception points follow successful downstaging.",
  "They follow a policy clock. The initial request and the first extension receive calculated MELD; only an extension after the first receives MMaT-3, and since each exception runs 90 days two periods elapse first, roughly six months. Policy states the score table, not a six-month rule, the rule changes without notice to this document, and no outcome evidence shows that the waiting construct selects better transplant candidates. MMaT is the median MELD at transplant for the donor hospital in that match run, not one national number.",
  "The current Policy 9 text on the day of the decision, the acquisition circle, and local policy where it is stricter.",
  "A named owner and a calendar date for re-verifying Policy 9 criteria against this document; listing dates against first exception request dates."],
 ["Checkpoint inhibitors before transplant are manageable with a washout.",
  "Kayali’s 52-patient pooled review concerns checkpoint inhibitors given after transplantation and cannot define a pre-transplant washout. Pre-LT cohorts provide observational timing evidence. AASLD advises discontinuation at least three months before LT, but no universally safe interval is validated and rejection can still occur. Transplant-specific review must document the interval, prior immune toxicity, alternatives and immunosuppression plan before exposure.",
  "Whether a graft may become available early, the agreed immunosuppression plan, the alternative bridging strategy, and transplant-specific review before the first dose rather than after.",
  "Every pre-transplant checkpoint exposure logged with the agreed washout, the date of the last dose, the date of transplant and the rejection outcome."],
 ["TACE is the standard of care for intermediate-stage HCC, grade A.",
  "The randomised base is two small trials. Llovet 2002 randomised 112 of 903 screened patients (12%) and was stopped at the ninth sequential inspection after 71 deaths against a planned 85 per comparison, giving a hazard ratio of 0.47 (95% CI 0.25 to 0.91) for chemoembolisation versus no anticancer treatment, with the single baseline imbalance, a lower bilirubin in the chemoembolisation arm, adjusted for after it was seen. Its bland embolisation arm achieved a similar response rate without a significant survival benefit (adjusted HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.31 to 1.04). Lo 2002 analysed 79 patients at one Hong Kong centre, relative risk of death 0.50 (0.31 to 0.81), with no benefit demonstrable in tumours over 5 cm or in unilobar portal vein obstruction. The Cochrane review that pooled the randomised embolisation trials found no survival benefit once trials with early stopping and co-interventions were excluded (HR 1.22, 95% CI 0.82 to 1.83) and none in trials at low risk of selection bias (HR 0.88, 0.71 to 1.10). The comparator in both trials was no anticancer treatment, which no longer exists.",
  "Selectivity achievable, portal flow, ALBI and liver-function trajectory, and whether a declared control or downstaging goal exists at all.",
  "Decompensation at 30 and 90 days after TACE; number of sessions per patient and liver-function change across them."],
 ["Drug-eluting-bead and conventional TACE are equivalent.",
  "Equivalence was never shown; superiority failed twice. PRECISION V was a phase 2 trial that missed its primary endpoint, 6-month objective response of 51.6% versus 43.5%, a difference of 8.1% (two-sided 95% repeated confidence interval minus 4.8 to 22.6), one-sided P = 0.11, with no time-to-progression or survival data at all and a fixed 150 mg doxorubicin dose against a body-surface-area-adjusted comparator. PRECISION ITALIA stopped for futility at 177 of a planned 214 patients: 2-year survival 56.8% versus 55.4% (P = 0.949) and median time to progression 9 months in both arms. The one reproducible difference is pain, in 22 of 89 (24.7%) after beads versus 63 of 88 (71.6%) after conventional TACE, with grade 3 pain in 0 versus 16 (18.2%).",
  "Selectivity achieved, operator familiarity, cost, and the pain burden the patient will carry.",
  "Objective response and decompensation by bead versus lipiodol technique, and post-procedural analgesia requirement."],
 ["Radioembolisation is an alternative to TACE in BCLC B.",
  "PREMIERE improved time to progression without a demonstrated survival difference, but 35 of its 45 patients were BCLC A. It stopped for slow accrual at 45 of a planned 124 patients with no prespecified interim analysis, so the hazard ratio of 0.122 rests on 12 progression events with a confidence interval of 0.027 to 0.557, and median overall survival was 17.7 versus 18.6 months (P = 0.99). Half the radioembolisation arm was Child-Pugh B at first treatment versus 24% in the TACE arm. TRACE, a single-centre phase II trial, improved time to progression and overall survival against DEB-TACE (median 30.2 versus 15.6 months, HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.82, whole intention-to-treat population, 85% BCLC B) but was stopped early at interim analysis with 72 of the 136 patients needed, and the TACE arm carried 5 grade 5 events including three definitely treatment-related septic deaths against one after radioembolisation, so the control arm may have been harmed rather than the treatment arm helped. This supports selected disease-control use, not proof of cure or superiority to resection or ablation.",
  "Unilobar versus bilobar distribution, shunt fraction, remnant volume, whether hypertrophy is a goal.",
  "Time to progression, decompensation at 90 days, downstaging rate."],
 ["Radiation segmentectomy is a curative-intent option for ablation-unsuitable solitary tumours.",
  "Single-arm data only, and the endpoints are imaging. RASER treated 29 patients with a solitary tumour of 3 cm or less: target-lesion complete response in 24 of 29 (83%), a sustained complete response after one treatment in 26 of 29 (90%), target-lesion progression in 3 of 29 (10%) and overall progression in 9 of 29 (31%) at a median follow-up of 691 days, read by one unblinded in-house radiologist with no comparator and 5 of 29 (17%) lost to follow-up. All 8 explants showed 100% necrosis of the target lesion, but 3 of those 8 livers held additional untreated HCC, one with vascular invasion. LEGACY is retrospective, 162 patients, median tumour 2.7 cm with 62% under 3 cm: best response of 88.3% (95% CI 82.4 to 92.4) by localised mRECIST falls to a confirmed 46.3% (38.8 to 54.0) by RECIST 1.1, and 45 patients (28%) went on to transplant or resection, so its 86.6% 3-year survival cannot be attributed to the radiation. Both studies were funded by the microsphere manufacturer.",
  "Segmental anatomy, tumour size, remnant volume, dosimetry feasibility, transplant timing.",
  "Complete response, local progression, and transplant explant pathology."],
 ["Lobar radioembolisation grows the contralateral lobe enough to make an unresectable patient resectable.",
  "Radiation lobectomy rests on one retrospective single-centre volumetric cohort of 83 patients, only 67 with HCC, selected post hoc from about 700 lobar treatments with no portal vein embolisation comparator. A future liver remnant above 40% was reached in 25 of 83 (30%), median maximal hypertrophy was 26% (range minus 14 to 86), and the 45% figure required more than 9 months of waiting, during which median Child-Pugh deteriorated from 6 to 7 and new left-lobe tumours appeared in 13 of 67 HCC patients (19%) at a median of 224 days. Only 11 of 83 patients (13%) reached surgery, 5 resections and 6 transplants. The remnant is a volume ratio with irradiated parenchyma in the denominator and no functional test was done, so the gain may overstate the safe remnant.",
  "How long the patient can wait, whether portal vein embolisation would be faster, functional rather than volumetric remnant assessment, and the risk of new contralateral disease during the interval.",
  "Remnant volume and function before and after, interval to operation, and the proportion who actually reach resection."],
 ["Personalised dosimetry is now the standard for radioembolisation.",
  "DOSISPHERE-01 is a phase 2 trial of 60 randomised and 56 treated patients, stopped at a planned interim analysis for efficacy on an unmasked investigator-read endpoint, the EASL response of a single index lesion at 3 months: 20 of 28 (71%) versus 10 of 28 (36%), P = 0.0074. Overall survival of 26.6 versus 10.7 months (HR 0.421, 95% CI 0.215 to 0.826) is a secondary endpoint resting on 14 deaths in the personalised arm, and progression-free survival, the harder endpoint, did not differ (HR 0.71, 0.39 to 1.30, P = 0.26). Ten of 28 patients in the personalised arm went on to curative resection versus one, so part of the survival difference is surgery. Entry required an index lesion of 7 cm or more and 30% hepatic reserve, and the authors state generalisability to lesions under 7 cm and to resin microspheres is untested. The sponsor makes the device.",
  "Index lesion size, hepatic reserve, whether an ablative tumour dose is achievable, and whether conversion to surgery is the actual goal.",
  "Prescribed and achieved tumour absorbed dose recorded for every treatment; response by dose band."],
 ["Radioembolisation is not a substitute for systemic therapy in advanced HCC.",
  "The position is right but the evidence behind it is weaker than it looks. SARAH gave an intention-to-treat overall survival of 8.0 versus 9.9 months (HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.41, P = 0.18) while 53 of 237 patients (22%) assigned radioembolisation never received it; per protocol the medians were identical at 9.9 months (HR 0.99, 0.79 to 1.24). SIRveNIB gave 8.8 versus 10.0 months (HR 1.12, 0.9 to 1.4, P = 0.36) with only 130 of 182 (71.4%) treated, and patients from 5 of its 11 countries flew to Singapore for treatment. SORAMIC was negative in intention to treat (HR 1.01, 0.81 to 1.25) with 47.2% of patients missing the allocated treatment or having major protocol deviations. All three used body-surface-area or manufacturer-recommended activity rather than personalised dosimetry, and SARAH's own dose-response analysis found median survival of 14.1 months when the tumour absorbed dose reached 100 Gy or more versus 6.1 months below it. The comparator in all three was sorafenib, which is no longer first line.",
  "Whether the disease is truly liver-dominant, the delay to the systemic start, dosimetry capability, and liver-function cost.",
  "Time from decision to systemic-therapy start; patients who received a liver-directed procedure instead of a first-line systemic combination."],
 ["SBRT controls HCC better than thermal ablation.",
  "The only randomised comparison enrolled 166 patients with a solitary recurrent HCC of 5 cm or less after curative treatment, and its primary endpoint was a composite local progression-free survival that counts death from any cause: HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.24 to 0.87), P = 0.014, 3-year rate 84.3% versus 67.3%. The arms reached that endpoint differently, 8 of 14 SBRT events being deaths without local progression against 7 of 27 for RFA, so the result turns on 14 local progression events. Progression-free survival (HR 0.76, 0.50 to 1.15, P = 0.190) and overall survival (HR 0.91, 0.37 to 2.22, P = 0.830, 19 deaths) were indistinguishable, and the advantage was significant only in tumours of 2 cm or less (HR 0.39, 0.17 to 0.89), not at 2 to 5 cm (0.58, 0.20 to 1.68, P = 0.310). The retrospective Michigan series pointing the other way, with the SBRT advantage growing with size, had channelled allocation: the SBRT group had a median of 2 prior liver-directed treatments versus 0 and better Child-Pugh. Overall survival was identical there too.",
  "Anatomical suitability for a percutaneous route, tumour size, uninvolved liver volume, prior radiation dose, and whether a bridge to transplant is intended.",
  "Local progression and liver-function change at 12 months by modality; proportion of SBRT cases chosen for anatomy rather than after ablation failure."],
 ["External beam radiotherapy gives survival comparable with resection and ablation in early HCC.",
  "The figures BCLC 2026 cites come from a retrospective individual-patient cohort with no resection, ablation or TACE arm: 4,913 patients from 30 of 96 eligible centres (31%), the centres identified because they had published favourable outcomes. Median overall survival was 6.8 years (95% CI 5.7 to 8.7) for BCLC-0, 4.6 (4.1 to 5.1) for BCLC-A and 3.6 (3.0 to 4.9) for BCLC-B, but 58% of the cohort was BCLC-C, 60% had been treated before, BCLC stage had to be re-adjudicated because reported staging was discordant, and treatment-naive BCLC-B patients survived 6.3 years, longer than treatment-naive BCLC-A, which is not a believable ordering. The proportional hazards assumption was formally violated in all four Cox models and the authors say their hazard ratios should be interpreted with caution. ASTRO's strong recommendation for EBRT as a potential first-line single therapy rests on single-arm and retrospective series; its own task force states no randomised trial has compared EBRT with thermal ablation or catheter-based therapy, and surgical oncologists published a formal dissent.",
  "Whether surgery, transplant or ablation has actually been excluded and why; uninvolved liver volume; prior dose; decompensation risk.",
  "Child-Pugh and ALBI change at 3 and 12 months after liver radiotherapy; proportion of EBRT cases in whom resection or ablation was never formally assessed."],
 ["Adding SBRT or radioembolisation to systemic therapy helps liver-dominant BCLC C.",
  "No randomised test against a modern immunotherapy backbone. RTOG 1112 missed its primary endpoint: median overall survival 15.8 months (90% CI 11.4 to 19.2) versus 12.3 (10.6 to 14.3), HR 0.77 (90% CI 0.59 to 1.01), one-sided P = .06, and significance appears only in the multivariable model (HR 0.72, P = .04). It needed 368 patients and 277 events, closed early in March 2021 and analysed 177 patients and 153 deaths at 65% power; 13 of 85 patients (15%) in the SBRT arm never started sorafenib and 19 of 92 (20.7%) controls later received radiotherapy. The Asan trial of TACE plus 40 Gy against sorafenib reported overall survival of 55.0 versus 43.0 weeks (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.98) as a secondary endpoint, but 90.7% of the sorafenib arm had crossed over by 24 weeks, so it compares two sequencing strategies, and it never reported how many of its 90 patients had cirrhosis. The neoadjuvant radiotherapy trial for portal vein tumour thrombus that ASTRO cites counted only tumour-related death, drew 157 of 164 patients from one hospital and cost 11% of patients their operation.",
  "Liver-dominant burden, symptom burden, uninvolved-liver volume, prior dose, time to systemic start.",
  "Time from decision to systemic-therapy start; hepatic progression-free survival."],
 ["SBRT is a reasonable option for residual disease after an incomplete TACE.",
  "One randomised trial of 40 patients at a single Italian centre supports it, against a planned 50, powered on an implausible hazard ratio of 0.18. One-year local control was 84% versus 23% (HR 0.15, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.4, P = 0.0002) and progression-free survival 9 versus 4 months (HR 0.43, 0.21 to 0.87), but distant recurrence-free survival did not differ and overall survival was identical at 31 versus 30 months (P = 0.472). The comparator was mostly bland embolisation, 15 of 19, not conventional or drug-eluting-bead TACE, and 10 of 19 control patients crossed over to SBRT. The parallel randomised comparison of SBRT with DEB-TACE as primary therapy, TRENDY, closed at 30 of 100 planned patients and was negative on its primary endpoint (time to progression HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.16 to 1.32, P = .15); its quoted 100% versus 54% local control is a post hoc per-protocol analysis, the prespecified comparison giving P = .075.",
  "Whether a viable target remains and is reachable, liver-function trajectory, prior dose to that volume, and what a well-selected TACE rechallenge would achieve.",
  "Local control and decompensation after consolidative SBRT; cases re-embolised versus irradiated after an incomplete first TACE."],
 ["Histotripsy met its endpoints in the HOPE4LIVER pivotal trial.",
  "It met a technical endpoint in a population that is not the one a tumour board would send for ablation. The co-primary endpoints were technical success, 42 of 44 treated tumours (95%, 95% CI 84 to 100) against a 70% performance goal that the authors say was agreed with the FDA for achievable enrolment and was not intended to identify a difference from existing therapies, and procedure-related major complications, 3 of 44 participants (7%, 2 to 18) against a 25% goal. Neither is tumour control. Only 18 of 44 participants (41%) had HCC, 4 of the 25 metastatic patients had more than 20 liver lesions, mean tumour diameter was 1.5 cm, the treatment zone averaged 3.6 cm, 38 of 44 tumours were in segments II to IV and none in segments VII or VIII. Technique efficacy had already fallen to 83% (30 of 36) at 30 days, and one grade 5 hepatic failure occurred in 44 participants despite the planned volume being achieved. The one-year update of 47 patients and 52 tumours reports freedom from local progression of 63.4% on the prespecified core-laboratory read against 90% on a post hoc read made once all imaging was available, with reader agreement of 70.8% to 84%; 12-month overall survival was 58.6% overall and 73.3% in HCC. FDA clearance for tumour destruction is a safety and performance determination.",
  "Acoustic window and target visibility, segment, device working range, and whether any established curative option would be displaced.",
  "Every histotripsy case in a prospective registry with the prespecified rather than post hoc local-control read; one-year local progression and liver-function change."],
 ["Three first-line immunotherapy combinations are interchangeable because none is ranked above the others.",
  "None has been compared with another, and each was tested against a different and now-superseded comparator, so the absence of a ranking is a gap, not a finding. IMbrave150 gave 19.2 versus 13.4 months against sorafenib (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.85) but its exploratory non-viral subgroup was imprecise (HR for death 1.05, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.63; median 17.0 versus 18.1 months), without proof of no benefit or a validated treatment-selection interaction, and only 422 of 1,447 real-world patients on tyrosine-kinase inhibitors (29%) would have met its eligibility. HIMALAYA gave 16.43 versus 13.77 months (HR 0.78, 96.02% CI 0.65 to 0.93) with no progression-free survival benefit at all (HR 0.90, 0.77 to 1.05), curves separating only after 9 months, and main portal vein thrombosis excluded. CheckMate 9DW gave 23.7 versus 20.6 months against lenvatinib or sorafenib (HR 0.79, 0.65 to 0.96) with crossing hazards, a piecewise hazard ratio of 1.65 (1.12 to 2.43) in the first 6 months, 12 treatment-related deaths against 3 with 11 of the 12 inside that window and 9 of them fatal hepatic events, a restricted mean survival difference of only 2.8 months (0.2 to 5.4) at 47 months, and Vp4 invasion excluded.",
  "Variceal and bleeding risk, aetiology, how much runway the patient has in the first six months, autoimmune history, and transplant intent.",
  "Early mortality at 6 months by regimen; variceal assessment documented before the first dose of atezolizumab-bevacizumab."],
 ["There is a second-line sequence after a first-line immunotherapy combination.",
  "There is no randomised evidence for any sequence after a modern combination; every agent on the list was tested after sorafenib, in a population that no longer exists, and each gain is small. CELESTIAL gave 10.2 versus 8.0 months (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.92) but stopped at 484 of 621 planned deaths (78%), with a hazard ratio of 1.11 in hepatitis C disease, grade 3 or 4 events in 68% and a median delivered dose of 35.8 mg against an intended 60. /* ---------- helpers ---------- */
const esc = s => String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({"&":"&","<":"<",">":">",'"':"""}[c]));
function refTag(id){ const r = REF[id] || NONPM[id]; return r ? r[0] : id; }
function refChips(ids){
  if(!ids || !ids.length) return "";
  return '<div class="refs">' + ids.map(id =>
    `<button class="refchip" data-ref="${id}" type="button">${esc(refTag(id))}</button>`).join("") + '</div>';
}
/* {{pmid|pmid}} inline markers become chips */
function expand(html){
  return html.replace(/\{\{([^}]+)\}\}/g, (m, ids) => refChips(ids.split("|")));
}

/* ---------- build stage buttons + answer ---------- */
const stageBtns = document.getElementById("stageBtns");
stageBtns.innerHTML = STAGES.map(s => `
  <button class="st" type="button" data-stage="${s.id}" data-tone="${s.tone}" aria-pressed="false">
    <span class="sname">${esc(s.name)}</span>
    <span class="sreq">${reqLabel(s.req)}</span>
    <ul class="scrit">${s.crit.map(c => `<li>${esc(c)}</li>`).join("")}</ul>
  </button>`).join("");

/* Collapsed by default: the stage reads as a list of options at rest, and the
   criteria, cautions and sources open on demand. */
function detail(o){
  const bits = [];
  if(o.pref)  bits.push(`<div class="optline"><span class="optlab">Preferred when</span><span>${esc(o.pref)}</span></div>`);
  if(o.avoid) bits.push(`<div class="optline bad"><span class="optlab">Caution / avoid</span><span>${esc(o.avoid)}</span></div>`);
  if(o.note)  bits.push(`<div class="recnote" style="margin-top:7px">${esc(o.note)}</div>`);
  const chips = refChips(o.refs);
  if(chips) bits.push(`<div style="margin-top:8px">${chips}</div>`);
  if(!bits.length) return "";
  const n = (o.refs||[]).length;
  const label = [o.pref||o.avoid ? "Criteria and cautions" : "", n ? n + (n===1?" source":" sources") : ""]
                .filter(Boolean).join(" · ");
  return `<details class="more"><summary>${esc(label)}</summary><div class="moreinner">${bits.join("")}</div></details>`;
}
function recHTML(r){
  const cls = LABELCLS[r.l] || "p-std";
  const flags = (r.flags||[]).map(f=>`<span class="flag">${esc(f)}</span>`).join(" ");
  const body = r.opts ? `
    <div class="opts">${r.opts.map((o,i)=>`
      <div class="opt">
        <div class="optn">${r.rank === false ? "·" : i+1}</div>
        <div style="min-width:0">
          <div class="optname">${esc(o.name)}${o.g?`<span class="grade ${o.g}">${o.g}</span>`:""}${(o.flags||[]).map(f=>`<span class="flag">${esc(f)}</span>`).join(" ")}</div>
          <div class="optwhen">${esc(o.when)}</div>
          ${detail(o)}
        </div>
      </div>`).join("")}</div>
    ${r.order?`<details class="more"><summary>How to choose among these options</summary><div class="moreinner"><div class="orderrule" style="border-top:0; margin-top:2px; padding-top:0">${r.order}</div></div></details>`:""}
    ${r.flagnote?`<details class="more"><summary>Decision requiring local approval</summary><div class="moreinner"><div class="callout amber" style="font-size:12.8px">${r.flagnote}</div></div></details>`:""}`
    : `<div>${esc(r.t)}</div>${detail(r)}`;
  return `<div class="rec">
    <div class="recmeta"><span class="pill ${cls}">${esc(r.l)}</span>${r.g?`<span class="grade ${r.g}">${r.g}</span>`:""}${flags}</div>
    ${body}
  </div>`;
}
function renderStage(id){
  const s = STAGES.find(x=>x.id===id);
  if(!s) return;
  document.getElementById("answer").innerHTML = RoadmapFlow.render(s,recHTML);
  RoadmapFlow.update(s);
  try{ localStorage.setItem("hcc.stage", id); }catch(e){}
}
/* Child-Pugh: five parameters, 1–3 points each */
const CP = ["cpBili","cpAlb","cpInr","cpAsc","cpEnc"].map(id=>document.getElementById(id));
function cpCalc(){
  const pts = CP.reduce((a,s)=>a + Number(s.value), 0);
  const cls = pts <= 6 ? "A" : pts <= 9 ? "B" : "C";
  document.getElementById("cpClass").textContent = "Class " + cls;
  document.getElementById("cpPts").textContent = pts + (pts===1?" point":" points");
  document.getElementById("cpNote").textContent = {
    A:"Preserved function. This does not establish portal pressure — see the portal hypertension assessment.",
    B:"Selected B may still be treated, but most pivotal systemic evidence is Child-Pugh A. B9 and above is rarely appropriate outside a trial.",
    C:"Stage D unless transplant can correct it — ask the transplant question before assigning the stage."
  }[cls];
}
CP.forEach(s=> s.addEventListener("change", cpCalc));
cpCalc();

/* Section-level folding: the page reads as its outline at rest. */
function setFold(id, open){
  const body = document.getElementById(id);
  const btn = document.querySelector(`[data-fold="${id}"]`);
  if(!body || !btn) return;
  body.hidden = !open;
  btn.textContent = open ? "Hide" : "Show";
  btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(open));
}
document.querySelectorAll("[data-fold]").forEach(b=>{
  b.setAttribute("aria-expanded","false");
  b.addEventListener("click", ()=> setFold(b.dataset.fold, document.getElementById(b.dataset.fold).hidden));
});
document.getElementById("expandAllSections").addEventListener("click", e=>{
  const b = e.currentTarget, open = b.dataset.open !== "1";
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-fold]").forEach(x=> setFold(x.dataset.fold, open));
  b.dataset.open = open ? "1" : "0";
  b.textContent = open ? "Collapse all sections" : "Expand all sections";
});
/* Opening a folded section from the top nav */
document.querySelectorAll("nav.sec a").forEach(a=>{
  a.addEventListener("click", ()=>{
    const id = a.getAttribute("href").slice(1);
    const map = {honest:"honestBodyWrap", ops:"opsBody", evidence:"evBody"};
    if(map[id]) setFold(map[id], true);
  });
});

document.getElementById("answer").addEventListener("click", e=>{
  const b = e.target.closest("#xpandAll"); if(!b) return;
  const open = b.dataset.open !== "1";
  document.querySelectorAll("#answer details.more").forEach(d=>{ d.open = open; });
  b.dataset.open = open ? "1" : "0";
  b.textContent = open ? "Collapse criteria and evidence" : "Expand criteria and evidence";
    b.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(open));
});
/* Changing stage must not move the page under the reader: the stage row and the
   answer are both in view on a laptop, and on a phone the answer panel sits
   directly below the row you just tapped. Only scroll when the panel is wholly
   off-screen, and then only far enough to bring its top into view. */
function selectStage(id){
  renderStage(id);
  const a = document.getElementById("answer");
  const r = a.getBoundingClientRect();
  if(r.top > window.innerHeight - 60){
    window.scrollBy({top: r.top - (window.innerHeight - 200), behavior:"smooth"});
  }
}

<section id="tree">
  <div class="sechead">
    <h2>The decision tree</h2>
    <p>Three questions in order. Every <b>yes</b> settles the stage; every <b>no</b> moves to the next question. Performance status and spread are therefore decided before tumour burden is ever asked. Choose any answer or any stage to see the full recommendation.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="tree">
    <div class="entry"><b>HCC confirmed</b> — LR-5 on multiphase CT or MRI in an at-risk liver; biopsy when imaging is indeterminate, decided at MDT. <b>Stage with</b> liver imaging and chest CT · ECOG · Child-Pugh and bilirubin · portal hypertension assessment · AFP. Nonresectability and transplant candidacy are assessed in parallel with the rest of staging, not after it.</div>

    <div class="refstrip">
      <span class="reflab">Reference</span>

      <details class="more"><summary><svg class="ricon" viewbox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="4" y="2.5" width="16" height="19" rx="2.5"></rect><rect x="7.5" y="6" width="9" height="3.5" rx="1"></rect><circle cx="8.5" cy="13.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="13.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="15.5" cy="13.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="8.5" cy="17.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="17.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle><circle cx="15.5" cy="17.5" r=".9" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></circle></svg>Child-Pugh</summary><div class="moreinner">
        <p class="small muted">Five parameters, 1–3 points each. <b>Class A 5–6 · Class B 7–9 · Class C 10–15.</b></p>
        <div class="cp">
          <label>Bilirubin (mg/dL)
            <select id="cpBili"><option value="1"><2</option><option value="2">2–3</option><option value="3">>3</option></select></label>
          <label>Albumin (g/dL)
            <select id="cpAlb"><option value="1">>3.5</option><option value="2">2.8–3.5</option><option value="3"><2.8</option></select></label>
          <label>INR
            <select id="cpInr"><option value="1"><1.7</option><option value="2">1.7–2.3</option><option value="3">>2.3</option></select></label>
          <label>Ascites
            <select id="cpAsc"><option value="1">None</option><option value="2">Mild, diuretic-responsive</option><option value="3">Moderate–severe or refractory</option></select></label>
          <label>Encephalopathy
            <select id="cpEnc"><option value="1">None</option><option value="2">Grade I–II</option><option value="3">Grade III–IV</option></select></label>
        </div>
        <div class="cpout"><span class="cpclass" id="cpClass">Class A</span><span class="chip" id="cpPts">5 points</span>
          <span class="small muted" id="cpNote">Preserved function. This does not establish portal pressure — see the portal hypertension assessment.</span></div>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:10px">In primary biliary cholangitis and primary sclerosing cholangitis the bilirubin bands are <4, 4–10 and >10 mg/dL. The roadmap also records ALBI and MELD 3.0; Child-Pugh alone does not drive allocation.</p>
      </div></details>

      <details class="more"><summary><svg class="ricon" viewbox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="5" r="2.6"></circle><path d="M12 7.8v7"></path><path d="M6.5 10.2h11"></path><path d="M12 14.8 8.5 21"></path><path d="m12 14.8 3.5 6.2"></path></svg>ECOG performance status</summary><div class="moreinner">
        <table class="minitab"><thead><tr><th style="width:52px">Grade</th><th>Definition</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>0</td><td>Fully active, able to carry on all pre-disease performance without restriction.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>1</td><td>Restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out work of a light or sedentary nature — light house work, office work.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>2</td><td>Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to carry out any work activities; up and about more than 50% of waking hours.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3</td><td>Capable of only limited self-care; confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>4</td><td>Completely disabled; cannot carry on any self-care; totally confined to bed or chair.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>5</td><td>Dead.</td></tr>
        </tbody></table>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:10px">Oken et al., Am J Clin Oncol 1982. <b>In this pathway ECOG 3–4 settles stage D, and cancer-related ECOG 1–2 is part of stage C</b> — record whether the limitation is from the tumour or the liver, because that distinction decides whether transplantation remains an option.</p>
      </div></details>

      <details class="more"><summary><svg class="ricon" viewbox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3.4"></circle><path d="M12 1.8v3.4M12 18.8v3.4M1.8 12h3.4M18.8 12h3.4"></path></svg>LI-RADS, in full</summary><div class="moreinner">
        <p class="small muted">CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 diagnostic algorithm and the v2024 treatment-response algorithms. <b>Applies only in the at-risk population</b> — cirrhosis of any cause, chronic hepatitis B, or current or prior HCC. OPTN class 5 criteria for listing are a separate system.</p>

        <div class="lrgrid">
          <div>
            <h4 class="eyebrow">The four major features</h4>
            <table class="minitab keys"><tbody>
              <tr><td>Nonrim APHE</td><td>Unequivocal enhancement in the arterial phase, in whole or in part, that is <b>not</b> rim-shaped.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>Nonperipheral washout</td><td>Visually assessed reduction in enhancement relative to liver, in whole or in part, from an earlier to a later phase — not peripheral.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>Enhancing capsule</td><td>Smooth, uniform, sharp border around most or all of the observation, unequivocally thicker or more conspicuous than around background nodules.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>Threshold growth</td><td>≥50% increase in size in ≤6 months.</td></tr>
            </tbody></table>
            <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:8px">Size is the fifth criterion and sets the row of the table; the three features other than APHE are what “additional major features” counts.</p>
          </div>
          <div>
            <h4 class="eyebrow">Other categories</h4>
            <table class="minitab keys"><tbody>
              <tr><td>LR-1</td><td>Definitely benign.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-2</td><td>Probably benign.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-3</td><td>Intermediate probability of malignancy.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-4</td><td>Probably HCC.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-5</td><td>Definitely HCC.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-M</td><td>Probably or definitely malignant, not HCC specific — targetoid appearance or other features favouring cholangiocarcinoma or a combined tumour.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-TIV</td><td>Tumour in vein: enhancing soft tissue within a vessel, whatever the parenchymal observation.</td></tr>
              <tr><td>LR-NC</td><td>Not categorisable because of image degradation or omission.</td></tr>
            </tbody></table>
          </div>
        </div>

        <h4 class="eyebrow" style="margin-top:16px">Diagnostic table — no nonrim APHE (absent, or rim / peripheral discontinuous)</h4>
        <table class="minitab"><thead><tr><th style="width:38%">Additional major features</th><th><20 mm</th><th>≥20 mm</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>0</td><td>LR-3</td><td>LR-3</td></tr>
          <tr><td>1</td><td>LR-3</td><td>LR-4</td></tr>
          <tr><td>≥2</td><td>LR-4</td><td>LR-4</td></tr>
        </tbody></table>

        <h4 class="eyebrow" style="margin-top:14px">Diagnostic table — nonrim APHE present</h4>
        <div class="minitabwrap"><table class="minitab"><thead><tr><th style="width:34%">Additional major features</th><th><10 mm</th><th>10–19 mm</th><th>≥20 mm</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>0</td><td>LR-3</td><td>LR-3</td><td>LR-4</td></tr>
          <tr><td>1</td><td>LR-4</td><td>LR-4 if capsule alone<br>LR-5 if washout or threshold growth</td><td>LR-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td>≥2</td><td>LR-4</td><td>LR-5</td><td>LR-5</td></tr>
        </tbody></table></div>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:8px"><b>An observation under 10 mm cannot be LR-5.</b> LR-5 requires ≥10 mm with nonrim APHE plus nonperipheral washout or threshold growth, or ≥20 mm with nonrim APHE plus any one additional feature.</p>

        <h4 class="eyebrow" style="margin-top:16px">Treatment response v2024 — use the algorithm that matches the treatment</h4>
        <div class="minitabwrap"><table class="minitab"><thead><tr><th style="width:26%">Category</th><th>Nonradiation — ablation, TACE</th><th>Radiation — SBRT, Y-90</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>LR-TR Nonviable</td><td>No lesional enhancement, or treatment-specific expected enhancement.</td><td>No lesional enhancement.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>LR-TR Equivocal</td><td>Enhancement atypical for treatment effect and not meeting viable criteria.</td><td><b>Does not exist</b> in the radiation algorithm.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>LR-TR Nonprogressing</td><td>—</td><td><b>Unique to the radiation algorithm.</b> Persistently enhancing, stable or decreasing — treatment effect rather than residual tumour. Observe with close follow-up; do not retreat on enhancement alone.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>LR-TR Viable</td><td>Nodular, mass-like or thick irregular enhancement in or along the treated lesion.</td><td>New or enlarging mass-like enhancement.</td></tr>
        </tbody></table></div>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:8px">Applying the nonradiation algorithm after radioembolisation or SBRT is a recurring and consequential error in this pathway — it turns expected delayed necrosis into a false call of residual tumour.</p>

        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:12px"><b>Source history.</b> This table is standard reference material, not taken from the roadmap, which cites the ACR documents without reproducing them. Verify against the ACR CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 core and the v2024 treatment-response algorithms before it is used for reporting.</p>
      </div></details>
    </div>

    <div class="qrow" id="qrow">
      <div class="q"><span class="arrowR">→</span><div class="qbox">
        <div class="qhead">ECOG 3–4, or Child-Pugh C and not a transplant candidate?</div>
        <div class="qans">
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="D"><b>Yes →</b> stage D · terminal</button>

      <div class="q"><span class="arrowR">→</span><div class="qbox">

        <div class="qans">

      <div class="q"><div class="qbox">
        <div class="qhead">With ECOG 0 and preserved liver function, what is the tumour burden?</div>
        <div class="qans">
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="0">Solitary ≤2 cm <b>→</b> stage 0</button>
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="A">Solitary any size, or ≤3 nodules each ≤3 cm <b>→</b> stage A</button>
          <button class="goto" type="button" data-goto="B">Multinodular beyond A <b>→</b> stage B</button>
        </div>
      </div></div>
    </div>

    <p class="small muted">Assess liver function before assigning stages 0–B. Child-Pugh B or decompensation needs individualized hepatology and transplant assessment; tumour burden alone does not establish an early stage or treatment eligibility.</p>

<section id="stage">
  <div class="answer" id="answer"></div>
  <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:10px">Stage migration is permitted when anatomy, biology, liver function, transplant strategy, comorbidity, access or patient goals make the stage default unsuitable — the reason must be recorded. It is not a licence to substitute a lower-evidence modality for a proven curative option.</p>
</section>

<section id="lrt">
  <div class="sechead">
    <h2>Liver-directed therapy</h2>
    <p><a href="../lrt/" style="display:inline-block;padding:10px 0;font-weight:700">Open the liver-directed therapy matrix across all five tumor types →</a></p>
    <p>Intent is assigned before a device is chosen. Curative intent means an attempt to eradicate all known cancer; it does not establish a cure rate. Local control, complete radiographic response, complete pathologic necrosis in a treated lesion, and overall survival are four different outcomes.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card" style="margin-top:16px">
    <h3>Choose treatment by its goal and suitability</h3>
    <p>Do not use a universal ablation → SBRT → Y-90 → TACE → HAI → histotripsy sequence. <b>An upfront alternative chosen because of anatomy or organ reserve is not a post-progression second line.</b> Bridge and downstaging preserve a later transplant or resection opportunity; conversion treatment is not itself the curative operation.</p>
    <p>Compare resection, local ablation and transplant where appropriate at multidisciplinary review, and record the intended outcome, why alternatives fit or do not fit, the systemic-treatment plan, the reassessment date and the next action. After progression or toxicity, restage and reconsider complete treatment rather than automatically repeating the same procedure.</p>
    <p class="small muted">The tiers below are a clinical synthesis of treatment intent. They are not the roadmap's A–D evidence grading system, and the two should not be read as equivalent.</p>

{id:"dx", name:"Diagnosis & staging", html:`
<div class="card">
  <h3>Surveillance and recall</h3>
  <p class="kicker"><span class="pill p-std">Standard</span> <span class="grade B">B</span>   Ultrasound plus AFP every six months for adults with cirrhosis and eligible chronic hepatitis B populations.</p>
  <p><b>Grade challenge.</b> v0.2 graded this A. Only one randomised trial has shown a mortality benefit for HCC surveillance, and it was conducted in a chronic hepatitis B population in China; the evidence in cirrhosis is observational and subject to lead-time and length-time bias. AASLD 2023 rates semiannual ultrasound plus AFP surveillance Level 2, Strong Recommendation. Grade B is the defensible label — this does not weaken the recommendation, but it should not be cited as randomised-trial-grade certainty when counselling patients or negotiating quality targets. {{15042359|37199193}}</p>
  <p><b>Recall.</b> US-1 continue six-month surveillance. US-2 subthreshold observation under 10 mm, repeat ultrasound and AFP in 3–6 months. US-3 positive, a rising or elevated AFP trigger, <b>or a visualisation score of C</b> → diagnostic multiphase contrast-enhanced MRI or CT. Visualisation score is recorded separately from the US category and is the trigger most often missed operationally. {{LIRADS}}</p>
  <p>Do not initiate or continue surveillance in patients for whom no HCC treatment, including transplant, would be offered. Record that decision rather than leaving surveillance orders open.</p>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Diagnostic categories</h3>
  <p class="kicker">LI-RADS applies only within the at-risk definition: cirrhosis of any cause, chronic hepatitis B, or current or prior HCC.</p>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table><thead><tr><th style="width:18%">Finding</th><th>System action</th><th style="width:7%">Grade</th></tr></thead><tbody>
   <tr><td><b>LR-5</b></td><td>Treat as HCC without routine biopsy after multidisciplinary imaging confirmation.</td><td><span class="grade A">A</span></td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>LR-4</b></td><td>Multidisciplinary review. Repeat or alternative contrast imaging at about three months, or biopsy when an immediate diagnosis would change management — transplant listing, or an imminent resection.</td><td><span class="grade B">B</span></td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>LR-3</b></td><td>Repeat CT or MRI in 3–6 months; escalate to tumour board sooner for growth, concerning AFP, transplant relevance, or discordant interpretation.</td><td><span class="grade B">B</span></td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>LR-M</b></td><td>Biopsy when feasible, because non-HCC malignancy changes the entire pathway. Coordinate tissue acquisition with pathology and molecular needs at the first pass.</td><td><span class="grade A">A</span></td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>LR-TIV</b><br><span class="small muted">tumour in vein</span></td><td>Tumour in vein contiguous with an LR-5 parenchymal mass in an at-risk patient may be managed as HCC with macrovascular invasion. Biopsy when the vein finding is isolated, when the parenchymal mass is not LR-5, or when bland thrombus cannot be excluded — the distinction changes both staging and transplant eligibility. v0.2 required biopsy for all tumour in vein; this is narrowed.</td><td><span class="grade B">B</span></td></tr>
   <tr><td><b>Non-cirrhotic</b><br><span class="small muted">without qualifying HBV risk</span></td><td>Pathologic confirmation is generally required; LI-RADS diagnostic certainty does not apply. Consider fibrolamellar HCC, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and metastatic disease.</td><td><span class="grade A">A</span></td></tr>
  </tbody></table></div>
  <p style="margin-top:12px"><b>Before any biopsy in a potential transplant candidate</b>, discuss the case with the transplant team first — sampling can affect transplant eligibility, and the transplant evaluation may settle the diagnostic question without it. <span class="pill p-std">Standard</span> <span class="grade D">D</span>. NCCN: “If patient is a potential transplant candidate, consider referral to transplant center before biopsy.” <span class="small muted">[original NCCN PDF p. 8]</span></p>
</div>
<div class="card">
  <h3>Required before a treatment decision</h3>
  <dl class="kv">
   <dt>Tumour</dt><dd>Number; largest viable diameter; segments; arterial enhancement and washout; LI-RADS category; infiltrative pattern; macrovascular invasion and its extent; extrahepatic disease; prior treatment map and response.</dd>
